title: Write it by hand, remember it longer
description: Typing is faster, and that is exactly the problem. Writing by hand is slow enough that your brain must choose what matters — and that choosing is where memory is made.
author: SparkKindly · AI-assisted

body.heading: Slowness is the mechanism
paragraphs: A keyboard lets you transcribe without thinking; a pen does not. Because handwriting cannot keep up with speech, the writer compresses, rephrases and connects — the very processing that moves an idea from hearing into knowing.

Studies comparing note-taking methods have repeatedly found the handwriting advantage for understanding, even when typists capture more words. More words, less thought, turns out to be the worse bargain.

body.heading: Use each tool for its job
paragraphs: This is not a war on keyboards. Type the final draft, the long document, the thing that must be searched and shared. Write by hand the first thinking: the summary, the plan, the three points you must not forget.
A practical rule: if you need to remember it next week, write it by hand once. The five slow minutes are the tuition your memory charges.

takeaway: Handwriting's slowness forces choosing and rephrasing — the processing memory is made of — so write by hand what you need to remember, and type what you need to share.
